claims.text: Systematic deviations from equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr compositions will produce measurable changes in mechanical properties.
The mechanical-property changes caused by off-equiatomic compositions arise from modified solid-solution strengthening and phase stability.
Changing the elemental makeup directly alters the alloy's microstructure and phase distribution.
The concentration of specific elements modulates solid-solution strengthening.
The concentration of specific elements modulates phase stability.
Changes in solid-solution strengthening and phase stability alter dislocation behavior.
Altered dislocation behavior changes overall mechanical performance.
Off-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloys will exhibit systematic variations in yield strength relative to the equiatomic baseline.
Off-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloys will exhibit systematic variations in hardness relative to the equiatomic baseline.
Off-equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr alloys will exhibit systematic variations in tensile performance relative to the equiatomic baseline.
The expected mechanical-property variations will have moderate effect sizes.
The effect size depends on the degree to which each element's percentage deviates from the equiatomic composition.
Excessive compositional deviations may induce secondary phases.
Secondary-phase formation may confound the relationship between composition and mechanical behavior.
Complex inter-element interactions and phase transitions at larger composition deviations may obscure the contribution of individual elements.
